rounds.name: Recruiter Screen
rounds.format: 30 min phone call with a Meta recruiter
rounds.focus: Background, motivation, and alignment with Meta's core values
rounds.evaluates: Basic fit, story clarity, and cultural alignment before investing further interview cycles.
questions: Walk me through your background and why you're interested in Meta.
Why product management, and why now?
What products have you shipped that you're most proud of?
What do you know about Meta's mission and the app/product you're interviewing for (Family of Apps, Reality Labs, etc.)?
What is your visa/work authorization status (relevant for India-based roles in Gurugram/Bangalore hiring)?
What are your compensation expectations and notice period?

rounds.name: Product Sense Interview
rounds.format: 45 min video call with a Product Manager (phone screen and/or onsite loop)
rounds.focus: User empathy, creativity, structured product design thinking
rounds.evaluates: Ability to identify user needs, generate and prioritize solutions, and reason about trade-offs for an ambiguous product design prompt.
questions: What is your favorite product and why?
How would you improve Instagram Stories?
Design a parking solution for Google Maps.
Create a tool to connect handymen with consumers.
Design a solution for contractors on an existing Meta platform.
Create a tool to connect volunteers with opportunities.
Design a map application for Meta.
How would you improve WhatsApp for small businesses in India?

rounds.name: Execution / Analytical Thinking Interview
rounds.format: 45 min video call with a Product Manager
rounds.focus: Goal-setting, metrics definition, prioritization, and data-driven decision-making
rounds.evaluates: Whether the candidate can define success metrics, diagnose a metrics problem, and prioritize a roadmap under constraints.
questions: Define a north star metric for Instagram Reels, and explain the trade-offs of your choice.
You're the PM for Facebook notifications on mobile. Why would Meta build this, and how would you measure success?
Define north star metrics for live events on Facebook.
Daily active users for a Meta product dropped 10% overnight — how do you investigate?
How would you prioritize a roadmap for a product with three equally compelling opportunities and limited engineering capacity?
How would you decide whether to launch a feature to 100% of users or run a staged rollout?
What metrics would you track for WhatsApp Business in an emerging market like India?

rounds.name: Leadership & Drive Interview
rounds.format: 45 min behavioral interview with a Product Manager or cross-functional leader
rounds.focus: Leadership without authority, resilience, ownership, conflict handling
rounds.evaluates: Whether the candidate can lead teams, handle setbacks, and drive execution — mapped against Meta's core values (move fast, be bold, focus on impact).
questions: Tell me about a product you're most proud of and your specific role in its success.
Tell me about a time you received harsh or critical feedback from your manager. How did you respond?
Tell me about a time you had to convince other stakeholders to move forward with your recommendation.
Describe a time you disagreed with your engineering lead. How did you resolve it?
Tell me about a time you failed. What did you learn?
Give an example of when you had to make a decision with incomplete data.
Tell me about a time you had to influence a peer or leader without formal authority.

rounds.name: Team Matching
rounds.format: Series of 30 min informal calls with hiring managers from different Meta orgs after passing the main loop
rounds.focus: Fit between the candidate's interests/background and specific open team needs
rounds.evaluates: Team-specific fit; this is not a pass/fail interview so much as a mutual-fit conversation, common at Meta for PM hires (including India-based roles in Family of Apps/Reality Labs/Payments) once the core loop is cleared.
questions: Which of our product areas are you most excited about and why?
What kind of ambiguity are you most comfortable operating in — 0-to-1 or scaling an existing product?
Tell me about your experience with the specific product area this team owns (e.g., monetization, growth, integrity, messaging).
What questions do you have about how this team operates day to day?
How do you feel about relocating or working with a distributed team across US and India time zones?
What would make you choose this team over another team you're also matching with?
How would your prior experience translate to the problems this specific org is solving right now?

rounds.name: Recruiter Screen + Technical Phone Screen
rounds.format: 30 min recruiter call, followed by a separate 45 min technical phone screen with a Meta TPM
rounds.focus: Background fit plus an initial gauge of technical depth tied to real programs
rounds.evaluates: Whether the candidate's program history has real technical substance worth advancing to the onsite loop.
questions: Walk me through a past project you led, focusing on the technical systems involved.
What requirements did you define for this project, and how did you prioritize them?
What tradeoffs did you face when designing or scoping this system?
How did you define success for this project? What metrics did you use?
Why did you (or your team) choose this architecture? What were the pros and cons?
What's the most technically complex program you've managed end-to-end?

rounds.name: Architecture, Product & System Design
rounds.format: 45 min whiteboard/video call with a Meta TPM or engineer
rounds.focus: Ability to reason about system architecture, scale, and trade-offs outside your own domain
rounds.evaluates: Technical depth and structured thinking when designing a large-scale system from scratch — not hands-on coding, but architecture judgment.
questions: Design Instagram.
Design WhatsApp.
Design an online chess game.
How would you design parking features on Google Maps?
Design a solution for the world of online learning.
Design Twitter.
Design a travel service.
Design YouTube.

rounds.name: Program Management / Program Sense
rounds.format: 45 min video call with a Meta TPM
rounds.focus: Program execution, prioritization, risk management, planning, and stakeholder influence
rounds.evaluates: Core TPM competencies: how a candidate kicks off, plans, de-risks, and drives a program to completion.
questions: Tell me about your program execution style.
Describe a situation where you changed a process to make it better.
Tell me about a time you took a strategic risk on a program.
How would you start a new program from scratch?
Tell me about a time you managed significant risk in a project.
How do you sunset a project or program?
Tell me about a time you negotiated with senior leaders over resourcing or scope.
Tell me about a time you dealt with conflicting stakeholder priorities.

rounds.name: Partnership / Cross-Functional Collaboration
rounds.format: 45 min behavioral interview with a cross-functional partner (engineering, product, or another TPM)
rounds.focus: Cross-functional collaboration, conflict resolution, and stakeholder management
rounds.evaluates: How the candidate builds trust and resolves friction with partner teams that don't report to them.
questions: Tell me about a time you had to build trust with a skeptical engineering team.
Describe a conflict between two teams you had to mediate.
Tell me about a time a partner team missed a commitment that affected your program. What did you do?
How do you handle a partner who consistently deprioritizes your program's needs?
Tell me about a time you had to say no to a partner's request.
How do you keep multiple partner teams aligned on a shared roadmap?

rounds.name: Behavioral & Leadership
rounds.format: 45 min interview with a senior TPM or cross-functional leader
rounds.focus: Cultural fit against Meta's core values and leadership maturity
rounds.evaluates: Whether the candidate embodies being bold, focusing on impact, learning from feedback/failure, and motivating others.
questions: Tell me about a time you made short-term sacrifices for long-term gains.
Give an example of a difficult stakeholder interaction and how you worked through it.
Tell me about a time you made a significant mistake on a program.
Tell me about a time you proposed an idea that wasn't initially agreed upon.
Tell me about a time you convinced someone to change their mind.
What motivates you, and how do you motivate the people around you?
Tell me about a time you dealt with significant ambiguity in a program's scope.
